# @kerfjs/ui

> Accessible, production-backed UI primitives for [kerf](https://github.com/brianwestphal/kerf)
> applications. Components are plain functions returning `SafeHtml`; the app owns
> state and wires stable `data-action` hooks once. This file orients an LLM to
> generate correct, good-looking kerf UI — it is not a catalog to browse.

```bash
npm install kerfjs @kerfjs/ui # kerfjs is a peer; Web Awesome is an optional peer
```

Import each component from its own subpath (`@kerfjs/ui/list-item`, `@kerfjs/ui/toolbar`,
…); the browser build pulls that component's reachable CSS automatically, so do not
maintain a central style list. Configure JSX with `"jsxImportSource": "kerfjs"`.
For a public subpath containing several visual components, use a folder with one
component per source file and one owned stylesheet per visual component. Keep its
compatibility entrypoints implementation-free: JavaScript/TypeScript only re-exports
the folder modules, and CSS only imports their owner stylesheets.

## The rule: components own their styles

Configure components through their typed props (size, density, inset,
presentation, `ToolbarConfig`, `PaneConfig`, …); never restyle one from outside.
No application or parent CSS may select a `.kui-*` class, a `[data-component]`
root, a `wa-*` element a Kerf component renders, or its `::part()`s, and no
writing another component's `--_kui-*` / `--kui-*` variables where a prop
exists. When a component adapts inside another, it styles itself in that
context in its own stylesheet. A missing prop is a component gap to report,
not a reason to override — and your own components follow the same rule.

## How to build a screen (retrieval order)

1. **Pick the component from the interface need**, not by appearance — read
   [component-selection.md](./docs/component-selection.md) (the problem→component
   matrix, with imports, wiring, ownership, and alternatives).
2. **Get exact signatures before emitting code** — read
   [public-api-signatures-v1.md](./ai/public-api-signatures-v1.md) (real prop names,
   callback shapes, disposer return types).
3. **Look up each component you use** in the
   [component reference index](./ai/components/README.md) — one line per
   entry — then read only those `ai/components/<id>.md` pages (1–7 KB each):
   use/avoid, imports and side effects, a link to exact props, legal parents,
   zones with their JSX prop and child count, app- and wiring-owned state,
   geometry, accessibility, the styling boundary (configure through props;
   never override internals), and `KUI-C###` diagnostics. Do not load the
   large JSON catalogs just to choose or compose components; the pages are
   generated from them.
   **Tools and mechanical checks** use the JSON sources instead: the
   [Machine-readable component catalog](./ai/component-catalog.json) (ids,
   exports, variants, `publicClasses`, relationships, side effects, and
   geometry ownership) — the canonical checked-in source; its schema is
   alongside it. Also load the
   consuming application's catalog extension when present; generate one from the
   [Consumer catalog extension schema](./ai/component-catalog-extension.schema.json)
   when app-owned components must participate in selection or alignment.
   A tool loads the [Composition catalog](./ai/component-composition.json) — a
   generated composition layer beside the component catalog, not a replacement
   for it — to mechanically evaluate parents, contexts, zones/cardinality,
   children, state, wiring (including the wiring-owned `stateAttributes` an app
   must never render or remove), responsive/layout/accessibility rules, and
   public boundaries. The component catalog stays the selection and delivery
   surface; the composition layer joins catalogs by `package:id`. Consumer
   composition catalogs use
   [the composition extension schema](./ai/component-composition-extension.schema.json).
   Load [compile-time contracts](./ai/compile-time-contracts-v1.json) for stable
   `KUI-T###` ids, exact declaration symbols, and the boundary between rejected
   source states and relationships that still require runtime/catalog checks.
   Before generating application UI, discover `.kerf-ui-profile.json` with the
   shipped [application profile API](./ai/application-ui-profile.mjs). Merge
   package defaults, workspace policy, then parent-to-child directory policy;
   honor its package-qualified preferences, approved theme/density, semantic
   tokens, layout conventions, and narrow source-located exceptions. Validation
   is catalog-aware per layer, including parent values later overridden by a
   child; synchronous hosts use [application-ui-profile-sync.cjs](./ai/application-ui-profile-sync.cjs).
   See the
   [workspace profile example](./docs/examples/application-ui-profile.json).
   A zone's optional `jsx.prop` is its only authoritative JSX binding; never
   infer one from the zone id. Use `children` for one homogeneous primary
   region and explicit named content prop slots for semantic positions or
   replacement content. These slots use the recursive `KerfUiContent` type:
   `SafeHtml`, runtime-empty boolean/nullish values, and readonly nested arrays.
   Put conditionals and mapped component arrays directly in them; do not add a
   `Fragment` only to satisfy types. Arbitrary strings, numbers, and signals are
   rejected unless a component explicitly exposes a text position such as
   `ListInsetText`. These are typed props, not native `<slot>` elements,
   wrapper slot components, or a generic `slots` object. Leave unresolved
   dynamic expressions unknown.
   Stable single-root Kerf UI components separately accept the explicit native
   `slot="name"` prop for light-DOM composition inside a custom element and
   preserve it across rerenders. Do not infer arbitrary native-attribute
   spreading from this narrow interop contract. `ResizableRegion` and
   `CollapsiblePanel` remain excluded because their optional restore controls
   make their output multi-root; `CollapsiblePanelToggle` remains slot-capable.
4. **When authoring a component gallery**, load
   [catalog-authoring.json](./ai/catalog-authoring.json), then follow its
   authoritative [Catalog demo authoring contract](./docs/catalog.md#catalog-demo-authoring-contract).
   Use its component/composition/recipe taxonomy and functional-group,
   importance, alphabetical-tie, and recipes-last ordering policy. Focused
   demos and recipes use public components plus `CatalogExample.viewport`,
   never local stylesheets, inline styles, or styling-only classes.
5. **Apply the rules below and in** [skill.md](./ai/skill.md).
6. **Before calling an integration complete**, run
   [`kerf-ui-doctor`](./docs/ui-doctor.md). Its portable JSON report merges
   profile/catalog, TypeScript, Kerf ESLint, and static analyzer diagnostics;
   CSS-adjacent component props are checked from catalog `cssValueProps`, so
   prefer its canonical shorthand or typed helper over raw CSS strings; a
   `--wa-color-{tone}-fill-loud` override without a governing `on-loud` (same
   or ancestor scope, possibly in a co-loaded stylesheet), or whose literal
   pair measures below 4.5:1, is review finding `KUI-L018` (set both); CSS that restyles a component
   (`KUI-L019`), touches its private `--_*` variables (`KUI-L020`), overrides a token a typed prop sets
   (`KUI-L021`), or styles it through a hook class on its root (`KUI-L022`) is an error: configure the
   component instead, and report a component gap when no prop exists; use `"ownership": "component"` with catalog `styleSources` to apply this boundary between an app's own components; repair source-located errors until exit 0. Use full mode for release gates;
   generated `dist`/`coverage`, dependency, cache, evidence, and nested-worktree
   directories are excluded consistently from every static stage.
   [`kerf-ui-analyze`](./docs/ui-analyzer.md) remains available when only static
   layout diagnostics are wanted; its review findings are a bounded human/AI
   review queue rather than an objective aesthetic score.
7. **Evaluate the running application** by explicitly enabling the doctor's
   browser stage or directly invoking
   [`kerf-ui-evaluate`](./docs/ui-evaluator.md). Preserve its `KUI-B###`
   browser evidence and screenshots; record hierarchy/rhythm/density/aesthetic
   ratings separately with a named reviewer rather than presenting them as
   objective assertions.

## Core rules (do the right thing)

- **Prefer a Kerf UI component over a Web Awesome component over a raw HTML
  tag**, using each for what it is good at. Never render a `Discouraged` Web
  Awesome element (`wa-dropdown`, `wa-button-group`, `wa-select`, `wa-tab-group`,
  `wa-icon`, …) directly; reach it only through the Kerf component that wraps or
  replaces it (`PopupMenu`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, `TabBar`,
  `LucideIcon`), and file a component gap rather than dropping to the raw tag.
- **Reach for the primitive, not for CSS.** The package is built to look right
  without an application customization layer. Before adding `padding`, `margin`,
  `width`, `height`, `border`, `background`, a wrapper card, or a decoration,
  check whether the component, pane, or content-item already owns it. Prefer a
  component prop — `FloatingToolbar inset`, `DisclosureArrow size`, `ListHeader
headingLevel`, `TokenSearchField clearIcon`, `ContentItem frame="framed"` for a
  visibly bounded content item — over overriding its `--kui-*` token. CSS for genuinely new structure
  belongs to the application-owned component that renders it and must not select
  nested Kerf or Web Awesome components.
- **Never double-inset.** A `.kui-pane` has no padding; its `.kui-content` children
  own the geometry (8px inline margin + 1px border + 8px padding). Render an
  ordinary surface-like child as `ContentItem` (`@kerfjs/ui/content-item`) with
  typed `frame` (`none`/`framed`) and `shape` (`rounded`/`pill`) props instead
  of hand-writing `<div class="kui-content-item">`. Do not add a
  container padding on top of a content-item's own margin — pick one owner. Use
  `.kui-content` for 24px major vertical rhythm.
- **Opt into document globals explicitly.** Import `@kerfjs/ui/document.css`
  once for border-box sizing, token-backed body/link presentation, and zero body
  margin. Put `.kui-app-root` on the one direct mount container only when a
  percentage-height shell needs the provided `html` → `body` → app-root height
  chain. The baseline is not part of `styles.css` or component browser imports.
- **Use compact layout options where needed.** `Text flush lineHeight="tight"`
  fits short dialog copy; `ValueTable density="compact"` reduces row spacing,
  with public row column, padding, and gap tokens for specific metadata layouts.
  `ToolbarText size="xsmall"` suits a dense rail heading. The
  `TokenSearchField` editor shrinks in narrow groups; its minimum width can be
  set with `--kui-token-search-editor-min-width`.
- **Label read-only field previews.** Use `FieldLabel` from `@kerfjs/ui/text`
  in `ListInsetControl sides="trl"` above a `ContentItem` value. Connect its
  id to the preview group's `aria-labelledby`; use the live control's own
  `label` while editing.
- **Use Toolbar zone options.** `responsive="trailing-priority"` moves an
  expanded trailing control to a full second row at `responsiveAt`; the leading
  title remains above it. Public leading-min-width, trailing-gap/justify, and
  per-zone inline-padding tokens cover app-specific toolbar geometry.
  In a stacked Toolbar, `ToolbarControlGroup placement="end"` places a collapsed
  search at its row's trailing edge; `sizing="fill"` gives its expanded state a
  full row and a reduced-motion-aware downward entrance.
  `--kui-toolbar-inset: 0px` removes an embedded Toolbar's outer padding and
  corresponding minimum-height allowance while preserving its zone gap and
  safe-area compensation.
- **Position region restore controls declaratively.** A ResizableRegion has a
  background token, `contentOverflow="visible"` for an anchored popup,
  top/bottom `restorePosition`, typed `restoreInset`, and
  `restorePlacement="inline"` for normal flow. FloatingToolbar also has
  `placement="inline"`, per-edge inset tokens, and `safeAreaInsets`.
- **Configure list rows through their APIs.** `ListItem density="spacious"`
  gives option rows more room. `multiline` wraps labels, with
  `multilineIconAlign="center"` when the icon should center on the whole copy.
  `divider` owns row separators and `state="drag-target"` paints the drop
  target. Public ListItem tokens set row, icon, label, and trailing geometry;
  ListHeader height, title padding, and border tokens tune section density.
  For a filled command list, scope `--kui-list-item-background`,
  `--kui-list-item-color`, `--kui-list-item-border`,
  `--kui-list-item-hover-background`, `--kui-list-item-hover-border`,
  `--kui-list-item-selected-background`, `--kui-list-item-selected-color`,
  and `--kui-list-item-selected-border` at the list or row boundary.
- **Use `Row` for horizontal and `List` for vertical layout.** Both expose
  physical `hAlign`/`vAlign` props and typed gaps. Row defaults to left/full,
  an `xs` gap, and no wrapping; List retains full/top and zero-gap defaults.
  Use canonical physical `textInsets` or `controlInsets` sides in
  `t`/`r`/`b`/`l` order; text geometry wins on overlapping sides.
  `ListInsetText` and `ListInsetControl` inset every side by default and accept
  the same `sides` grammar for selective edges.
  List additionally supplies
  optional typed `gap`, `flex`, vertical scrolling, and canonical
  `dividerSides` (`t`/`r`/`b`/`l` order). It adds no list semantics; children own
  those, and only one bounded region should own scrolling. Pass a finite spacing
  shorthand (`gap="xs"`, `gap="m"`) or a complete `CssLength` from the CSS-free
  `@kerfjs/ui/css-values` builders; raw CSS strings are rejected. Use `flex()`
  for List flex, typed lengths for Skeleton geometry, and
  foreground colors for choice icons: `uiColor()` with an `*-on-*`/text token
  or `foregroundColorVar()`; fill tokens such as `uiColor('success-fill-quiet')` do not
  type-check. These brands are intentionally
  not interchangeable; rows use classes/tokens/props rather than raw `style`.
- **Use `Grid` for equal-width columns.** Set a fixed positive `columns` count
  or typed `minColumnWidth` for automatic container-width collapse, never both.
  The app owns the outer width and child semantics; use custom CSS grid for
  asymmetric/intrinsic tracks and `ResizableRegion` for adjustable boundaries.
  `Grid.gap` and `Grid.flex` use the same typed grammars as Row.
  For selectable document tiles, use `selectionMode="multiple"` and a required
  `ariaLabel`, with `ContentItem selectionMode="multiple"` children. Wire
  `wireContentItems` for spatial arrow navigation and Enter/Space activation.
- **Give a layout root `fill`, not a frame `Pane`.** A Row, List, or Grid that
  is the sole layout root of a definite-height parent takes its full height
  with `fill` and carries safe `data-*` markers through `rootAttributes`.
  Inside a flex layout use `flex` instead.
- **Keep Web Awesome on the shared inset tiers.** `webawesome.css` uses
  `--kui-wa-control-inset` (8px controls/items) and
  `--kui-wa-surface-margin` / `--kui-wa-surface-inset` (8px around/inside
  Accordion, Card, Details, Callout, and Include), while
  plain Details keep their body flush while plain Accordion items inset both
  trigger and body, framed Details use the 16px container inset only on the
  trigger, and framed Accordion items use it on both regions;
  `--kui-wa-container-inset` keeps Tab Panel at 16px. Dialog body and footer use
  the surface (8px) and container (16px) tiers respectively, independent of the
  dialog's shared `--spacing`. Override the tier at the narrowest useful scope
  instead of restyling individual shadow parts.
  Filled badges use each semantic variant's quiet fill with normal text for
  WCAG-AA compact-copy contrast. Override
  `--kui-wa-badge-filled-background` and
  `--kui-wa-badge-filled-foreground` as a contrast-safe pair instead of adding
  host selectors.
  When a dialog provides another dismissal affordance, add `hide-actions` to
  the `wa-dialog` host; the theme hides its directly exported `header-actions`
  part without an unsupported chained `::part()` selector.
  Checkbox and Radio Group option regions also receive the shared 8px inline
  outer inset because those groups have no bordered field shell. The Color
  Picker trigger receives the same inset for the same unbordered geometry.
  Slider's complete interactive region uses the shared 8px logical inline outer
  inset without shifting its already-aligned label.
  Known Date's Month/Day/Year captions and bordered text-like field hints align
  with field values at the shared 9px border-plus-padding inset. OTP Input's
  label uses the same uppercase xs/650 treatment and its label and hint share
  that 9px alignment.
- `Select` requires a visible `label` or an `ariaLabel` for a visually hidden
  accessible name. Set `multiple` with an array `value` for any number of
  choices: the popup stays open while choices toggle and closes on an outside
  press or Escape, and the closed control summarizes the chosen labels. A
  toolbar filter menu adds `selectedPresentation="icon-only"` and a fixed
  `triggerIcon`: the trigger shows that icon plus a count badge while any
  choice is chosen, and its accessible name ends with the chosen labels.
  Set `caret={false}` on an icon-only toolbar Select to make a round trigger;
  a custom `renderSelected` icon stays centered, and the default keeps the
  visible caret.
  `SelectChoice.disabled` keeps an unavailable option visible but unselectable;
  `disabledReason` adds its tooltip. For multiple selects, opt in to
  `selectAllLabel` and `clearLabel` footer buttons to select enabled choices
  or clear the value through ordinary change events. The app owns the updated
  controlled value and localized action labels.
  Icon-only Selects (single or multiple) and icon-only `PopupMenu`s show an
  `aria-hidden` Web Awesome help tag repeating that name (and a Select's
  choice) on hover and keyboard focus, hidden while the popup is open; the
  register import installs it, so do not add a `title` or tooltip of your own.
  The same installer tags an icon-only `<button>` or link inside a
  `ToolbarControlGroup` named by `aria-label` (no visible text or `title`);
  import `@kerfjs/ui/help-tags/register` once when a toolbar has such buttons
  but no registered Select or PopupMenu.
  The package names the internal combobox, including custom
  selected content; consumers do not need shadow-DOM naming workarounds.
  Import `select/register` once for the canonical animation lifecycle: stale
  close/show completions cannot override a later request. Consumers must not
  repair popup timing or anchor placement; raw Web Awesome selects stay native.
  Use `hint` for supporting text below the control and `placeholderText` only
  for the empty value inside it; loading placeholders retain the visible hint.
- **Trust the defaults.** Render a control at its natural size and color (a
  `LucideIcon` is 24px); if it looks wrong, fix the surrounding layout, not the
  control. Never force a component's width/height to size it — that leaves a halo
  or a stretched oval.
- **Toolbars hold only `ToolbarText` and `ToolbarControlGroup`.** Never put a bare
  button, input, link, or loose markup in a `leading`/`center`/`trailing` zone.
  Wrap every control — `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, a collapsible
  `TokenSearchField`, Web Awesome controls — inside a `ToolbarControlGroup`. For an
  ordinary icon/action control inside the group use a **plain `<button>`** (the
  group styles it fully) — that is the default; reach for `wa-button` only when you
  need a Web Awesome feature. A toolbar popup menu is a `PopupMenu`
  (`@kerfjs/ui/popup-menu`, registered once via `@kerfjs/ui/popup-menu/register`)
  in a `single` `ToolbarControlGroup` with `nestedDropdown`; never hand-write
  `wa-dropdown` markup for a menu. Let the group size the trigger from its icon,
  localized text, and caret. `PopupMenu` items also support nested `submenu`
  actions, headings, dividers, checked or trailing choice marks, danger tone,
  and disabled reasons; nested headings/dividers stay out of keyboard choices;
  use `context` with `openPopupMenuAt`/`closePopupMenu` for pointer-anchored row
  menus. Do not force a dropdown or button width. Nothing
  wraps inside a group: an icon sits beside its label on one row, and a
  `ToolbarText` is one ellipsized line unless you opt into `wrap`/`maxLines`. A
  Select or PopupMenu trigger drops its focus ring while its popup is open and
  the ring follows the control's shape; never add ring CSS. Compact
  mixed groups keep standard item padding and raised selected chrome without an
  internal separator; the selected item paints over the outer border. For an
  avatar control, set `content="avatar"` and `avatarImage` on the group instead of
  inserting an `img`; a lone control paints the group and a multi-button group
  paints only its pressed highlight. Dividers earn their place: a `Toolbar`
  draws none by default and pinned chrome gets its line from scroll state (see
  the scroll-divider rule below); never fake one with a border or pad below a
  divider to make it look right.
- **Use one direct toolbar composition for panel/dialog/page headings.** Put an
  optional icon in a `ToolbarControlGroup`, an extra-large `ToolbarText` directly
  in the leading zone, and actions in a trailing group. Supporting copy is
  app-owned content below. Do not create a private heading wrapper or restyle the
  toolbar. A narrow peripheral rail or drawer, where extra-large would truncate
  at its minimum size, names itself with the default `ToolbarText` size.
  `ToolbarText size="xlarge-fixed"` keeps the 20px `--kui-font-l` heading step;
  `xlarge` retains the responsive page-title clamp.
- **Use `Text` for ordinary semantic headings, paragraphs, and inline secondary
  text outside toolbar title zones.** Omit `variant` for the default `p`, pass
  `h1`–`h6` based on the document outline, or use `variant="span"` inside a row,
  label, or table cell without adding box geometry. Independently compose `tone="quiet|danger"`,
  `size="compact|large|xlarge"`, and `font="monospace"` for supporting, error,
  compact, prominent, display, and code roles instead of global utility classes. It passes native attributes
  through; block variants own the standard transparent border plus item padding, while `span` owns none. Keep
  toolbar titles on `ToolbarText` and list-aligned bare prose on `ListInsetText`.
- **Space by the five-step scale, by relationship not by eye.** `0`
  `--kui-space-none`, `4px` `--kui-space-2xs`, `8px` `--kui-space-xs` (inside a
  group), `16px` `--kui-space-m`, `24px` `--kui-space-l` (between major differing
  regions). 12px/32px are off-scale exceptions. Prefer direct `Row.gap`/`List.gap`
  shorthands for repeated rhythm; use `Spacer` for one typed empty width/height
  or flexible main-axis gap. Use `space`, `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `lengthVar`, and
  `calc(plus(...))` for typed runtime composition. `remify()` is source-CSS only.
- **Keep nested highlight corners concentric.** Inset hover and selection surfaces
  follow the owning control's pill or rounded shape; their radius is the outer
  radius minus `--kui-layout-highlight-inset`. Do not give an inner highlight an
  unrelated radius.
- **Panes share one child-owned geometry.** Sidebars, main areas, inspectors, and
  dialogs all render `Pane`: an unpadded `.kui-pane` (optional header, one
  scrolling `.kui-pane__content`, optional footer). Never write a component's
  anatomy classes onto your own element to recreate it (`KUI-L103`); only
  the catalog's `placeableClasses` (layout utilities, `.kui-app-root`,
  `.kui-content-item` on a non-div carrier) belong there. A visible pane owns
  its collapse control (the last control of its last group); a hidden pane's
  restore moves to the adjacent main toolbar's matching edge — no icon-only
  rail — and a collapsed drawer's restore sits in the bottom toolbar or a
  `FloatingToolbar` beside the drawer, near where its effect appears. Align
  text to text and icons to icons across a pane; a border is decoration, never
  the alignment anchor. Keep one scroll owner per region.
- **Dividers between pinned chrome and scrolling content are scroll state.**
  Toolbars draw no divider by default. Call `wireScrollDividers(appRoot)`
  (`@kerfjs/ui/wire-scroll-dividers`) once and keep its disposer: every `Pane`
  with `chromeDividers="scroll"` then draws the line under its header only while content is scrolled beneath
  it and the line over its footer only while more content lies below (never
  when the content fits), every `NavStack`'s top chrome and bottom toolbar and
  every `TabScaffold` bar do the same around the active view or scene, and
  every `TabBar` marks each side of its strip with tabs scrolled out of view. Configure a pane with `chromeDividers`
  (`scroll` for a plain pane by default, `always` for a sunken pane by default,
  or explicit `scroll`, `always`, `none`), and a `NavStack` or `TabScaffold`
  with its own `chromeDividers` (same values; a `SplitView` forwards it through
  `compactStack`); name app-owned chrome in `targets`.
  Never add a border, or a permanent `dividerSides`, to fake one.
  While a side overlay is open (a Workbench rail overlay, a `wireSidebar` compact
  overlay, an overlay `CollapsiblePanel` or horizontal `ResizableRegion`), the
  layout hides the covered work area's `FloatingToolbar`s and restore corners
  itself (unfocusable, out of the accessibility tree) until it closes — do not
  hide them from overlay state yourself.
- **State and behavior live in the app.** Components take semantic `data-action`
  strings and controlled values; wire them once with `delegate()`/`delegateActions()`
  or the disposer-returning `wire…` helpers, and own domain copy, transport, and
  policy in a thin adapter. Every element must earn its place — cut chrome, labels,
  and readouts that do not help a person decide or act.
- **App state is domain/persisted; helpers own only ephemeral mechanics.** Keep
  navigation stacks, tab selection and order, pane sizes, and `collapsed`/`expanded`
  disclosure flags in the app — they are data or persisted layout, and the app reads
  them to render. The `wire…` helpers own the _ephemeral_ parts: `wireNavStack` the
  content-slide, per-view top/bottom chrome cross-fade, and focus move/restore
  (mark a preferred new-view target with `data-nav-focus`), `wireTabBars` the
  overflow autoscroll, drag preview, and
  replacement focus after controlled automatic tab activation,
  `wireResizableRegions` the live drag preview, `wireScrollDividers` the
  scroll-state attributes from which a `Pane` draws its chrome dividers and a
  `TabBar` its overflow dividers; they report committed changes via
  callbacks. For a tab-local action plus a separate far-edge action, set
  `TabBar trailingPlacement="adjacent"`, put the local action in `trailing`, and
  the workspace action in `end`; the component keeps both visible while its tab
  list shrinks and scrolls, without application descendant CSS. Each action
  zone accepts one ToolbarControlGroup or a standalone `wa-button` for its own
  Web Awesome chrome. Managed
  TokenSearchField clear also preserves open state and replacement
  editor focus before the next input task, so shortcut-letter typing stays in search.
  Select All deletion does the same; deletion
  restoration finishes before the next keystroke rather than on a delayed frame.
  Persist both query and remaining tokens read from an edited field; change
  `revision` to replace unmanaged DOM-owned text programmatically, or call
  `model.replace({ query, tokens })` for a model-managed field. In grammar-assisted
  search, a model rule's `suggest(input, state)` receives current committed tokens
  so suggestions can omit selected values; one-argument callbacks still work.
  A sibling helper can call `model.commit(value)` for the active `name:` prefix
  even when that value is not suggested; invalid values and missing prefixes
  leave state unchanged.
  The one richer case is `wireTokenSearchFields`, which manages the
  collapsible field's expand/collapse/focus by default (on, per-behavior opt-out) and
  exposes the `expanded` signal on its handle — bind it in render or hand in your own
  via `collapsible.signals`. Do not hand-roll open/collapse/focus that helper
  provides; but do keep a plain disclosure toggle (a one-line boolean the app already
  renders from) in the app. For real-app composition it also offers a focusout
  keep-open exception (`data-token-search-keep-open` regions or `collapsible.keepOpenOn`,
  so a sibling suggestions/date popover does not collapse an empty field), opt-in
  atomic-chip keyboard (`keyboard`: Backspace/Delete remove the adjacent chip via
  `onRemoveToken`, ArrowRight moves the caret past a trailing chip), and an
  `onEdit({id, editor, event})` input callback (the `InputEvent` lets you gate on `inputType`/`data`) — so the app can drop its own keydown/input
  boilerplate while still owning parsing and controlled token state.
- **Placeholder loading state, don't rebuild it.** For a value or component that is
  still loading, set `placeholder` on the component (`Select`, `ListHeader`,
  `ListItem`, `ValueTableRow`, `SegmentedControl`, `StateBanner`,
  `AppTab`, `ToolbarText`, `ListActionRow`): it renders its real chrome with value
  slots as subtle **unanimated** skeleton blocks and interactivity disabled. Only
  unknown values change: a placeholder is never dimmed or styled as disabled (a
  control you disabled keeps its live disabled tone), so a parent composes a
  faithful loading view (e.g. an inspector) without hand-rebuilding markup.
  Component-drawn chrome stays live: a `ListItem` or `ListActionRow` keeps its
  `busy` spinner while its `status` (and a `ListItem`'s `trailing`) content
  become skeletons. Use the standalone `Skeleton` for a custom slot. Prefer it over `wa-skeleton`
  (the pure-Kerf primitives avoid Web Awesome), and never animate it — use
  `LoadingSpinner` for known busy activity instead. Set its `size` prop to a
  named icon step or positive pixel number when the inherited 1em is unsuitable.
- **Keep ListItem content inside the row.** The rounded `ListItem` root clips
  overflowing label, status, and dormant trailing content. Set `multiline` when
  the primary label should wrap; use `ListActionRow` instead when trailing content
  must be interactive.
- **Dialog bodies are lists by default.** Compose rows and sections in `List`,
  use `DialogSurface bodyInset="none"` when those children own their geometry,
  and wrap bare prose in `ListInsetText` so it shares the standard list gutter
  without stacking a second body inset.
- **Use a StateBanner badge only for compact supporting status.** Pass the
  optional string `badge` for a terse count or status beside the title. It
  inherits the banner tone and is announced with the banner, so keep its text
  meaningful and never rely on color alone.
- **Configure StateBanner copy and action placement.** `copyLayout="stacked"`
  puts detail below the title and badge; `actionPlacement="below"` gives the
  action a separate trailing row. The inline defaults remain compact.
- **Size a Select through its API.** `triggerWidth` chooses `fit-content`,
  `max-content`, or `fill`; `--kui-select-trigger-max-width` caps it. For custom
  selected text, use the public color, font-size, and font-weight tokens; the
  closed value ellipsizes when space runs out. `presentation="title"` gives a
  rail view heading a 36px bold, flush-start trigger and adjacent caret;
  `focusRingInset` keeps its ring inside clipping ancestors.
- **Configure application tabs at their owners.** AppTab's `icon-only`
  presentation keeps `name` accessible, `labelMaxWidth` ellipsizes a long name,
  `nameOverflow="visible"` shows the full name during inline loading, and
  `dropTarget` highlights a drag-over without changing selection. `attention`
  uses `--kui-app-tab-attention-color`. TabBar's public
  `--kui-tab-bar-strip-*` tokens set compact strip geometry.
  Set `pinned` on the first AppTab to keep it visible within a scrolling
  tablist; it remains in keyboard order. Use `--kui-app-tab-pinned-background`
  for the surrounding surface and keep that backdrop opaque.
- **Use `Badge` for compact non-interactive metadata.** Configure its semantic
  tone, appearance, shape, and size instead of creating badge CSS in an app or
  consuming component. Use a real button or link for interactive content.
  For new content without a count, use the text-free `size="dot"` form: it
  takes no children, and needs a `label` (announced as an image) or
  `ariaHidden` when its owner announces it. A `TabScaffold` tab shows the dot
  with `badge: true` plus its required `badgeLabel`.
- **Use `Chip` for removable tags.** Give the native remove button a delegated
  `removeAction` and a specific `removeLabel`; the application updates the tag
  list. `itemId` identifies the chip to the action handler. `size="compact"`
  gives a 20px chip and 16px remove button; `disabled` disables removal.

## Public exports

`Badge`, `LucideIcon`, `DisclosureArrow`, `Toolbar`, `ToolbarControlGroup`, `ToolbarActionLink`, `FloatingToolbar`, `ToolbarText`, `Text`,
`ListItem`, `ListActionRow`, `ListHeader`, `ListInsetControl`,
`ListInsetText`, `SegmentedControl`,
`Select`, `TokenSearchField` (+ `readTokenSearchField`, `placeTokenSearchCaret`,
`wireTokenSearchFields`), `AppTab`, `TabBar` (+ `wireTabBars`, `reorderTabs`),
`wireScrollDividers` (scroll-state dividers for every `Pane`, `NavStack`,
`TabScaffold`, and `TabBar`),
`ResizableRegion` (+ `wireResizableRegions`), `StateBanner`, `EmptyState`,
`LoadingSpinner`, `Skeleton`, `ValueTable`, `ValueTableRow`. Whole-screen layouts (opt-in,
tree-shakeable, declarative with `wire…` helpers; the browser build of each layout
subpath loads its CSS and that of the components it renders, and a companion
CSS subpath remains for pipelines without the `browser` condition):
`NavStack`, `SplitView`, `Workbench`, `TabScaffold`, driven by `deviceClass()` from
`@kerfjs/ui/device-class`. For a standalone collapsible rail/drawer outside a full
shell, `@kerfjs/ui/collapsible-panel` (`CollapsiblePanel`, `CollapsiblePanelToggle`)

- `@kerfjs/ui/wire-sidebar` (`wireSidebar`: toggle, focus, compact overlay, persistence; a compact overlay starts closed and opens only on a user action, and `inlineCollapsed` declares a panel's inline default).
  `@kerfjs/ui/catalog` is another opt-in shell — a
  `Catalog` component + `wireCatalog` helper for building a component-gallery catalog
  (collapsible category sidebar + preview stage + resources footer, with an opt-in
  transparent-bound and margin geometry overlay plus focus-preserving active-row
  reveal for long desktop sidebars) from your own
  entries; controlled/stateless like the layouts. For any Catalog demo, follow
  the [authoritative authoring contract](./docs/catalog.md#catalog-demo-authoring-contract)
  rather than inferring structure from the shell or private CSS.
  `@kerfjs/ui/webawesome` is a
  type-only boundary for `wa-*` JSX; `@kerfjs/ui/select/register` and the CSS are the
  declared side effects.

## Reference

- [skill.md](./ai/skill.md): the full rule set + a common-mistakes table (the shipped AI skill).
- [design-philosophy.md](./docs/design-philosophy.md): why kerf UI is shaped this way — the decision principles behind the rules above.
- [layout.md](./docs/layout.md): the pane/content-item geometry, public roles/tokens, and the spacing scale.
- [component-contract.md](./docs/component-contract.md): what a component owns vs. what the app owns.
- [accessibility.md](./docs/accessibility.md): keyboard and ARIA contracts per component.
- [recipes.md](./docs/recipes.md): production compositions (app shell, list-detail dialog, composer form, …) as copyable references.
- [workbench.md](./docs/workbench.md): the `Workbench` multi-panel shell, its collapse policies, and opt-in `resizable` panels driven by `wireWorkbench` (`@kerfjs/ui/wire-workbench`: drag, keyboard, min/max, persistence, compact suspension), the `mainMinSize` / `mainMinHeight` work-area minimums (default 320px wide beside any inline rail, 120px tall above the drawer) that resizable panels stop at and inline panels shrink around, and a panel's `responsiveOverlayAt` (`narrow` / `compact`, rails and the bottom drawer) that presents it as an overlay below a Workbench container breakpoint without a device-class check; a panel given its `collapsed` signal is a transient overlay (collapsed on entering the breakpoint, takes focus and keeps Tab inside while open, closed by Escape or an outside press, focus returned; `dismissOverlays`), and overlays are exclusive by default (opening one closes the others; `exclusiveOverlays: false` opts out).
- [app-layouts.md](./docs/app-layouts.md): choosing `NavStack`/`SplitView`/`Workbench`/`TabScaffold` by data + interaction + device, and dialog presentation, plus the safe-area model (surfaces paint through unsafe areas; content pads only the edges it reaches; `Pane.safeAreaEdges` for app-owned arrangements, `Toolbar.safeAreaEdges` for an app bar or bottom bar at a screen edge).
- [webawesome-theme.md](./docs/webawesome-theme.md): the optional Web Awesome theme; catalog coverage means themed-and-supported, not preferred (prefer the Kerf primitive when one exists). The UX sidebar visibly tags superseded and exceptional Web Awesome choices as `Discouraged`; Popup remains an available conditional positioning primitive.
- [ai/components/README.md](./ai/components/README.md): the generated per-component markdown reference — the assistant entry point over both JSON catalogs.
- [component-catalog.json](./ai/component-catalog.json) + [component-catalog-extension.schema.json](./ai/component-catalog-extension.schema.json) + [catalog-authoring.json](./ai/catalog-authoring.json) + [public-api-signatures-v1.md](./ai/public-api-signatures-v1.md) + [webawesome-jsx-signatures-v1.md](./ai/webawesome-jsx-signatures-v1.md): machine-readable selection facts, a reusable app-component extension contract, Catalog authoring discovery, and exact signatures.
- [compile-time-contracts-v1.json](./ai/compile-time-contracts-v1.json) + [type-contracts.md](./docs/type-contracts.md): stable compile diagnostics, packed-declaration proof, migrations, and explicit non-goals.
- [README.md](./README.md): package overview and the component subpath table.
